message.content:
**Answer**

It’s not possible to declare a winner with the information supplied.  
In Texas Hold’em each player uses **any combination of their own two “hole” cards plus the five community cards** (flop, turn, river) to make the best possible five‑card poker hand.  

Because the community cards were never revealed, there are many different ways the showdown could play out:

| Scenario | Possible outcome |
|----------|------------------|
| Board gives everyone a flush – e.g., ♠7♠9♦J♥T → Alex has a spade ace‑high flush, Robert gets a heart Q‑high flush, Steve gets a spade 5‑high flush, Sam gets nothing special. Alex wins. |
| Board gives a full house involving one of the lower pairs – e.g., ♥8♥8♦8♣K♠Q → Robert would win with three queens over his ten. |
| Board contains four of a kind – e.g., ♦A♦A♦A♦K♠Q → whoever holds an Ace beats anyone else. |

Without knowing those five community cards, the relative strength of the hands remains indeterminate. To find the actual winner you’d need the complete set of seven cards per player (or at least the community cards), then evaluate each hand according to standard Texas Hold’em rankings.
